    Reproducibility and Corpus Certificates

    Source: vignettes/reproducibility-and-certificates.Rmd
    reproducibility-and-certificates.Rmd

    Why certificates?

    Every bibliometric analysis starts with a corpus, but most analyses don’t document how the corpus was built. scimapR’s corpus certificates solve this: they are structured YAML documents that record the corpus hash, the steps behind the corpus and the local files it was built from, so that another researcher can check a corpus against them and run its searches again.

    library(scimapR)
corpus <- sm_example_corpus(seed = 42)

    Provenance tracking

    Every record in a scimapR corpus knows where it came from:

    head(sm_provenance(corpus))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 8
#>   work_id    source    source_id_external fetch_date          query       engine
#>   <chr>      <chr>     <chr>              <dttm>              <chr>       <chr> 
#> 1 W000000001 synthetic NA                 2026-10-26 19:22:25 sm_example… native
#> 2 W000000002 synthetic NA                 2026-10-26 19:22:25 sm_example… native
#> 3 W000000003 synthetic NA                 2026-10-26 19:22:25 sm_example… native
#> 4 W000000004 synthetic NA                 2026-10-26 19:22:25 sm_example… native
#> 5 W000000005 synthetic NA                 2026-10-26 19:22:25 sm_example… native
#> 6 W000000006 synthetic NA                 2026-10-26 19:22:25 sm_example… native
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: scimapR_version <chr>, prompt_hash <chr>

    Corpus hashing 

    sm_hash_corpus(corpus)
#> [1] "61c0637eede72e86bf489cf7d8a27949789b82485ea6646cc707da9ec1945bb6"

    Creating a certificate 

    cert <- sm_certificate(corpus)
#> ✔ Certificate created. Corpus hash: 61c0637eede7
str(cert, max.level = 1)
#> List of 20
#>  $ certificate_version: chr "1.0"
#>  $ created            : POSIXct[1:1], format: "2026-10-26 19:22:25"
#>  $ scimapR_version    : chr "0.4.0.9000"
#>  $ r_version          : chr "4.6.1"
#>  $ platform           : chr "unix"
#>  $ corpus_hash        : chr "61c0637eede72e86bf489cf7d8a27949789b82485ea6646cc707da9ec1945bb6"
#>  $ hash_version       : int 2
#>  $ n_works            : int 200
#>  $ n_authors          : int 80
#>  $ n_institutions     : int 0
#>  $ n_references       : int 1869
#>  $ year_range         : int [1:2] 2015 2024
#>  $ question_id        : chr NA
#>  $ queries            :List of 1
#>  $ provenance_summary :List of 1
#>  $ screening_summary  : list()
#>  $ embedding_info     :List of 13
#>  $ local_inputs       : tibble [0 × 9] (S3: tbl_df/tbl/data.frame)
#>  $ is_locked          : logi FALSE
#>  $ metadata           :List of 2
#>  - attr(*, "class")= chr "sm_certificate"

    Verifying a certificate 

    result <- sm_verify_certificate(corpus, cert)
result$pass
#> [1] TRUE
result$checks[, c("check", "expected", "actual", "status")]
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>   check          expected         actual           status
#>   <chr>          <chr>            <chr>            <chr> 
#> 1 corpus_hash    61c0637eede72e86 61c0637eede72e86 pass  
#> 2 n_works        200              200              pass  
#> 3 n_authors      80               80               pass  
#> 4 n_institutions 0                0                pass  
#> 5 n_references   1869             1869             pass

    Local input files

    A corpus built from local files, such as a database snapshot, an institutional export or an affiliation dictionary, records each file with its SHA-256 hash. sm_corpus_from_tables(inputs = ) registers the files the tables come from; sm_register_input() adds any other file.

    tracker <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
writeLines(c("doi,unit", "10.9999/example.1,Unit A"), tracker)
corpus <- sm_register_input(corpus, tracker, role = "publication tracker",
                            builder = "R/01_import.R::read_tracker")
cert <- sm_certificate(corpus)
#> ✔ Certificate created. Corpus hash: 61c0637eede7
sm_verify_certificate(corpus, cert)$checks[, c("check", "status")]
#> # A tibble: 6 × 2
#>   check                      status
#>   <chr>                      <chr> 
#> 1 corpus_hash                pass  
#> 2 n_works                    pass  
#> 3 n_authors                  pass  
#> 4 n_institutions             pass  
#> 5 n_references               pass  
#> 6 input:file2ed9142f0107.csv pass

# once the file changes, its check fails
cat("10.9999/example.2,Unit B\n", file = tracker, append = TRUE)
sm_verify_certificate(corpus, cert)$pass
#> [1] FALSE

    A file that verification cannot find is reported as "not checked", with a warning; its relative path is looked for in base_dir, in the folder of the certificate file and in the working directory. sm_rebuild_from_cert() replays the recorded searches of OpenAlex, PubMed and Crossref, but it cannot replay local files or file reads: for a corpus built only from them it stops and names the files and the code that read them.

    Saving and loading 

    tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
sm_save_corpus(corpus, tmp)
#> ✔ Corpus saved to /tmp/Rtmp6clkXC/file2ed93afac199.rds
loaded <- sm_load_corpus(tmp)
nrow(loaded$works)
#> [1] 200

    Snapshot and diff 

    snap_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
sm_snapshot(corpus, snap_path)
#> ✔ Corpus snapshot saved to /tmp/Rtmp6clkXC/file2ed926d17711.rds.
#> ℹ Size: 122K | Hash: 61c0637eede7

    Citation 

    sm_cite_corpus(corpus)
#> Corpus assembled using scimapR v0.4.0.9000 on 2026-10-26. Contains 200 works by 80 authors (2015-2024). Data sources: synthetic. Corpus hash: 61c0637eede7.

    Locking a corpus 

    locked <- sm_lock(corpus, reason = "Final version for publication")
#> ✔ Corpus locked.
#> ℹ Reason: Final version for publication
locked$metadata$is_locked
#> [1] TRUE

# sm_refresh(locked)  # This would error -- corpus is locked
